rhs_question_text:
A café is setting up a star network.

Draw a network diagram containing five laptops, two printers and one switch. Label all devices and show how they are connected. [3]
rhs_marking_guidance: Five clearly labelled computers, two printers and one switch; links form the required star configuration centred on the switch; no additional devices or links that change the topology.
rhs_examiner_insight: Some candidates omitted device labels, drew an extra router or server, or added links that made their diagram resemble a mesh.
original_question_summary: Draw network with computers printers and switch

rhs_question_text:
A school is considering using a star topology instead of a mesh topology for its network.

Explain one benefit and one drawback of choosing the star topology. [2]
rhs_marking_guidance: Valid benefit, such as simpler expansion or reduced cable requirements; valid drawback, such as dependence on the central switch or its additional cost.
rhs_examiner_insight: Commonly credited responses noted easier addition of a computer and the network's dependence on its central device.
original_question_summary: Compare star and mesh topology

rhs_question_text:
An office has several laptops connected to a switch in a star network.

Describe three functions performed by the switch when devices communicate across the network. [3]
rhs_marking_guidance: Switch links devices for LAN communication; receives frames; learns or uses MAC addresses in an address table; forwards data to its destination; unknown destinations may be flooded.
rhs_examiner_insight: Some candidates described hub-style broadcasting or confused switches with servers; stronger responses explained MAC-address learning and targeted forwarding.
original_question_summary: Describe role of switch in star network

rhs_question_text:
An airport has a computer network connecting devices within a single terminal building.

State two characteristics that make this network a LAN rather than a WAN. [2]
rhs_marking_guidance: Local geographical coverage; infrastructure owned and managed by the organisation rather than external providers; dedicated local hardware; connects local devices rather than remote networks.
rhs_examiner_insight: Most candidates mentioned the small geographical area. OCR emphasised that LAN and WAN are not distinguished by how many computers they contain.
original_question_summary: Identify two features that distinguish a single-building LAN from a WAN

rhs_question_text:
A hospital is planning to install a mesh network.

Describe two characteristics of a mesh network topology. [2]
rhs_marking_guidance: Devices have connections to other nodes; there are multiple possible routes between nodes; no central switch is required for topology management.
rhs_examiner_insight: Students sometimes confused a physical mesh of links with a client-server software arrangement or incorrectly described a central controlling device.
original_question_summary: Describe mesh network topology

rhs_question_text:
An airport is considering a mesh network instead of a star network.

Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using a mesh topology. [4]
rhs_marking_guidance: Benefit example: alternate routes reduce the effect of a failed link, with an explanation. Drawback example: extra wired connections are cumbersome or costly, with an explanation.
rhs_examiner_insight: Many identified fault tolerance, but fewer explained a disadvantage. Some incorrectly discussed client-server software instead of physical network connections.
original_question_summary: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of mesh versus star
Explain benefits of adding Wi-Fi alongside wired connections

rhs_question_text:
A hotel has noticed that its network performance changes throughout the day.

Explain how bandwidth and the number of connected users can affect network performance. [4]
rhs_marking_guidance: For bandwidth: identify its increase/decrease, then explain the resulting transmission/performance change using simultaneous data transfer. For users: identify increased/decreased concurrent use and explain its effect through shared bandwidth or traffic.
rhs_examiner_insight: Some only defined bandwidth or said performance would improve without stating whether bandwidth had increased. Others omitted the reason for slower performance with more users.
original_question_summary: Explain bandwidth and concurrent user effects on network performance

rhs_question_text:
A sports centre is considering using cloud storage for its files.

Describe five potential drawbacks of using cloud storage. [5]
rhs_marking_guidance: Possible drawbacks include dependence on an Internet connection, reduced control over provider security and location, ongoing costs, provider outages, loss of access, and uncertainty about backup or ownership.
rhs_examiner_insight: Candidates often identified Internet dependence. Better answers recognised loss of control over a provider's security or storage arrangements; OCR also corrected confusion between Wi-Fi and Internet access.
original_question_summary: Describe drawbacks of cloud storage for a youth centre

rhs_question_text:
A museum visitor enters www.example.org into a web browser.

Describe how DNS helps the browser find the IP address needed to access the website. [4]
rhs_marking_guidance: Browser may check a cached record; DNS resolves the supplied domain via an address lookup (and may consult another DNS); the IP address is returned to the browser/computer.
rhs_examiner_insight: Some wrote that the URL went to a web server rather than DNS, or said DNS returned the address to the person rather than the browser. Others omitted what DNS actually looks up.
original_question_summary: Describe resolution of website URL to IP address
